chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him), and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and a group of my scholars (may Allah have mercy on them), narrated from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from some of our companions, who said:

Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I have been informed that some people who went to visit al-Husayn (peace be upon him) carried with them baskets containing halawah (sweetmeats) and akhbisah (a type of sweet bread/pastry) and similar foods. If they had gone to visit the graves of their loved ones, they would not have carried these with them.

key_terms.السُّفَرَ: Baskets or containers for carrying food
key_terms.الْأَخْبِصَةُ: A type of sweet bread or pastry
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنَ (ع): Imam al-Husayn, son of Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.قُبُورَ أَحِبَّائهِمْ: The graves of their loved ones/relatives

ai.seo_question: What food etiquette is recommended when visiting the shrine of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) according to Kamil al-Ziyarat?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) observes that visitors to Imam al-Husayn’s shrine bring elaborate foods like sweets and pastries, unlike when visiting ordinary relatives' graves, highlighting the unique spiritual status of the Imams. This distinction underscores the concept of *ziyarah* as an act of reverence and devotion to the divine representatives, rather than a mere social visit or funeral rite. The hadith serves as a reminder to approach the shrines with the appropriate etiquette befitting the presence of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. My father, ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain and all of my scholars narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Abī Khalaf, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from ‘Ali ibn Ḥakam, from some of our companions, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: I have been informed that some people go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) carrying different kinds of food with them, including AKHBISAH and other similar deserts. Verily if they had gone to the graves of their loved ones, they would not have taken any of these (things) with them.
